results.title: Sage Research Methods - Document Analysis
results.content: Similar to other methods of analysis in qualitative research, document analysis requires repeated review, examination, and interpretation of the data in order to gain meaning and empirical knowledge of the construct being studied. Document analysis can be conducted as a stand-alone study or as a component of a larger qualitative or mixed methods study, where it is often used to triangulate findings gathered from another data source (e.g., interview or focus group transcripts, observation, surveys). This entry explores the method of using documents as data and describes the two primary types of data. Documents of all types can be useful for the researcher in uncovering insights, developing theory, and gaining a greater understanding of the topic of study. There are many types of documents that can be used, which include both primary and secondary sources of data. Primary types of data are documents that provide a first-hand account of an event or occurrence, without interpretation or analysis.

results.title: Quantitative vs Qualitative Research: Key Features and Steps
results.content: Qualitative Research: Data Collection, Analysis, and Management Qualitative research focuses on exploring and understanding human experiences, meanings, and social processes within their natural contexts. A Guide to Understanding Methodological and Functional Differences in Data Collection Tools Comparison Between Questionnaire and Scale in 11 Points In scientific research, distinguishing between a questionnaire and a scale is essential to ensure accurate selection of data collection tools and to achieve study objectives. Data Analysis in Scientific Research: A Statistical Framework for Understanding Phenomena, Testing Hypotheses, and Generalizing Results Statistical data analysis in scientific research is a systematic process aimed at transforming raw data into interpretable information that contributes to understanding studied phenomena, testing hypotheses, and deriving generalizable conclusions. This process begins with identifying the type of data (quantitative or qualitative), followed by selecting appropriate statistical methods based on the study design, variable nature, and sample size.
